blurb: Choose shorter or longer paddles between the County Road 45 landing, Medford, Kroghs Landing and Teepee Tonka Park. DNR notes that spring and early summer usually offer better water levels; shallow rocky channels and snags can make later trips difficult. These listings begin below Owatonna Dam and Clinton Falls.

sections.takeOut: Straight River Medford City Park Access
sections.difficulty: Moving water; rocky channels and snags possible
sections.notes: A shorter paddle from the county carry-in to Straight River Park in Medford. This launch is below Clinton Falls. Arrange a vehicle shuttle and check for low water, snags and bridge debris.
sections.routeReview: Approximate agency river-course overview. Exact landing connections, current obstructions and alternate channels are not mapped.

putInAccess.sourceName: Steele County — Straight River Canoe Landing
putInAccess.note: The unchanged agency coordinate falls in the river beside a wooded bank. County and DNR sources establish the public carry-in, but the exact shoreline connection is obscured. Keep an approximate area.
putInAccess.directions: Use the signed county canoe landing at 5218 North County Road 45, south of Medford. Carry boats along the public approach to the river. This access starts below Clinton Falls; identify the approach while arranging your shuttle.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: City of Medford — Straight River Park
takeOutAccess.note: The city confirms canoe/kayak access and the DNR lists a trailer launch. The agency point is at the wooded shoreline beside the approach, without a clear water-edge ramp end. Current DNR map mile 17.1 differs from inventory 17.2.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the public river access in Straight River Park in Medford, off 4th Avenue NW. Follow the signed approach beside the park; check parking and ramp conditions during your shuttle. This is separate from Frank Woodfill Wildlife Refuge farther upstream.

sections.difficulty: Class I–II rapids near the former mill
sections.notes: Paddle north from Medford to Kroghs Landing. Identify the take-out during your shuttle; it is just downstream of the former mill site. This is a moving-water trip with a rapid near the end.
sections.routeReview: Approximate agency river-course overview. Exact landing connections, current obstructions and alternate channels are not mapped. The former Walcott Mill Dam rapids are on this trip; the line does not select a passage through them.

takeOutAccess.note: The agency point is at the bank beside the public turnout. A worn approach is visible, but the exact landing edge is not distinct enough for a precise pin. Retain the original coordinate as an approximate access area.

sections.takeOut: Straight River Teepee Tonka Park Access
sections.difficulty: Moving water; rocky channels and snags possible
sections.notes: Start below the former Walcott Mill Dam rapids and continue past River Bend Nature Center to Faribault. The DNR map marks a large midstream boulder near mile 6.9. Finish at the designated park carry-in, before the separate downstream Bridge-to-Park access.
sections.routeReview: The agency line differs from the visible channel near a railway crossing below Kroghs Landing. Access areas and published planning distances remain available; no dotted course is shown for this trip.
